translation_en: ‘Abd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us: Bahz narrated to us: Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrated to us: Sa‘id ibn Mina’ narrated to us, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade muzabanah, muhaqalah, mukhabarah, and selling fruit until it began to redden. I asked Sa‘id what that meant. He said: “It reddens and yellows, and some of it can be eaten.”

‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Umar al-Qawariri and Muhammad ibn ‘Ubayd al-Ghubari narrated to us—and the wording is ‘Ubayd Allah’s. They said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr and Sa‘id ibn Mina’, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade muhaqalah, muzabanah, mu‘awamah—one of them said it means selling for several years—thunya, and mukhabarah, and he granted a concession for ‘araya.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and ‘Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us: Isma‘il, Ibn ‘Ulayyah, narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet, with a report like it, except that he did not mention the phrase explaining mu‘awamah as selling for several years.

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Majid narrated to us: Rabah ibn Abi Ma‘ruf narrated to us: I heard ‘Ata’ narrating from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade leasing land, selling it for several years, and selling fruit until it was ripe.
Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to me: Hammad, Ibn Zayd, narrated to us, from Matar al-Warraq, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah forbade leasing land.

‘Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, whose title was ‘Arim, Abu al-Nu‘man al-Sadusi, narrated to us: Mahdi ibn Maymun narrated to us: Matar al-Warraq narrated to us, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever has land should cultivate it; if he does not cultivate it, he should let his brother cultivate it.”

Al-Hakam ibn Musa narrated to us: Hiql, meaning Ibn Ziyad, narrated to us, from al-Awza‘i, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said: Some of the Messenger’s Companions had surplus land. The Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever has surplus land should cultivate it or grant it to his brother. If he refuses, let him keep his land.”

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Mu‘alla ibn Mansur al-Razi narrated to us: Khalid narrated to us: al-Shaybani informed us, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade taking rent or a share for land.

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever has land should cultivate it. If he cannot cultivate it and is unable to manage it, he should grant it to his Muslim brother and not rent it to him.”

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us. Sulayman ibn Musa asked ‘Ata’, “Did Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah narrate to you that the Prophet said: ‘Whoever has land should cultivate it or let his brother cultivate it, and should not rent it’?” He said, “Yes.”
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from ‘Amr, from Jabir, that the Prophet forbade mukhabarah.

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha‘ir narrated to me: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Majid narrated to us: Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrated to us: Sa‘id ibn Mina’ narrated to us: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever has surplus land should cultivate it or let his brother cultivate it, and do not sell it.” I asked Sa‘id what “do not sell it” meant. He said, “Renting it.”

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir, who said: In the time of the Messenger of Allah we practiced mukhabarah and received a portion of the harvest and such. The Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever has land should cultivate it or let his brother plow it; otherwise, let him leave it.”

Abu al-Tahir and Ahmad ibn ‘Isa both reported from Ibn Wahb. Ibn ‘Isa said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Hisham ibn Sa‘d narrated to me that Abu al-Zubayr al-Makki told him: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say: In the time of the Messenger of Allah, we took land on condition of a third or a fourth, using irrigation channels. The Messenger stood and said: “Whoever has land should cultivate it. If he does not cultivate it, he should grant it to his brother. If he does not grant it to his brother, let him keep it.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us: Abu ‘Awanah narrated to us, from Sulayman: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Jabir, who said: I heard the Prophet say: “Whoever has land should give it away or lend its use.”

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha‘ir narrated it to me: Abu al-Jawwab narrated to us: ‘Ammar ibn Ruzayq narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, with this chain, except that he said: “Let him cultivate it or let a man cultivate it.”

Harun ibn Sa‘id al-Ayli narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: ‘Amr, Ibn al-Harith, informed me that Bukayr told him that ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Salamah narrated to him, from al-Nu‘man ibn Abi ‘Ayyash, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah forbade leasing land. Bukayr said: Nafi‘ also told me that he heard Ibn ‘Umar say: We used to lease our land, then stopped when we heard the hadith of Rafi‘ ibn Khadij.
Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Abu Khaythamah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade selling bare land for two or three years.

Sa‘id ibn Mansur, Abu Bakr ibn Shaybah, ‘Amr al-Naqid, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from Humayd al-A‘raj, from Sulayman ibn ‘Atiq, from Jabir, who said: The Prophet forbade selling crops for several years. Ibn Abi Shaybah’s narration says, “selling fruit for several years.”

Al-Hasan al-Hulwani narrated to us: Abu Tawbah narrated to us: Mu‘awiyah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, that Yazid ibn Nu‘aym informed him that Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah told him he heard the Messenger of Allah forbid muzabanah and fields. Jabir said: “Muzabanah is exchanging fruit for dates, and fields means leasing land.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from ‘Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: I asked Ibn ‘Abbas about selling date palms. He said the Messenger of Allah forbade selling them until some of their fruit had been eaten—or could be eaten—and until it was weighed. I asked what “weighed” meant. A man present said, “Until it is estimated.”

Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’, narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nu‘m, from Abu Hurayrah, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Do not buy fruits until their ripeness becomes apparent.”

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah narrated to me—and the wording is Harmalah’s. They said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who narrated to me from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, that Abu Hurayrah said the Messenger of Allah said: “Do not buy fruit until its ripeness appears, and do not buy fruit in exchange for dates.” Ibn Shihab said Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar told me, from his father, from the Prophet, the same.
Ibn ‘Umar said: Zayd ibn Thabit narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah granted a concession for selling ‘araya. Ibn Numayr’s narration adds: “that they be sold.”

Muhammad ibn Rafi‘ narrated to me: Hujayn ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, that the Messenger of Allah forbade muzabanah and muhaqalah. Muzabanah is selling the fruit of date palms for dates; muhaqalah is selling crops for wheat and leasing land for wheat. Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah informed me, from the Messenger of Allah, that he said: “Do not buy fruit until its ripeness appears, and do not buy fruit for dates.” Salim said: ‘Abd Allah told me, from Zayd ibn Thabit, from the Messenger of Allah, that afterward he granted a concession for selling an ‘ariyyah for fresh dates or dried dates, and did not grant a concession for anything else.

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from Zayd ibn Thabit, that the Messenger of Allah granted the owner of an ‘ariyyah permission to sell it for its estimated amount of dates.

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, who informed me that Nafi‘ heard ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar relate that Zayd ibn Thabit told him the Messenger of Allah granted a concession for an ‘ariyyah, allowing a household to take its estimated amount in dates so they could eat the fruit fresh.
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: I heard Yahya ibn Sa‘id say that Nafi‘ informed him, with this chain, with a report like it.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated it to us: Hushaym informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, with this chain, except that he said: “An ‘ariyyah is a date palm given to a group, and they sell its estimated yield for dates.”

Muhammad ibn Rumh ibn al-Muhajir narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar. Zayd ibn Thabit narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah granted a concession for selling an ‘ariyyah for its estimated amount in dates. Yahya said: An ‘ariyyah is when a man buys the fruit of date palms for his household to eat fresh, paying its estimated amount in dates.
